newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Short calls rolled forward in Railtrack.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Short calls rolled forward in Railtrack.

text.p: UK equity options attracted some brisk business on Tuesday as underlying shares were buffeted in a generally weak stock market, dealers said.
Many of the larger deals -- especially in the FTSE 100 index options -- were volatility trades or the rolling forward existing positions.

Under the latter category in railways operator Railtrack, 2,000 June 580 calls were bought back at 62p and a new short position created by selling 2,000 September 580 calls at 76p in the hope of capturing option premiums from time decay and decreasing volatility.
At 1345 GMT, Railtrack shares were up a penny at 640-1/2p.
In satellite broadcaster British Sky Broadcsating, a near-month straddle was believed to have been bought back and converted into a short strangle.
The closing deal involved involved buying back 200 June 600 puts and calls at 38p and 4p each and the long strangle consisted of buying 200 September 550/600 puts/calls at 26p/23p.
At September expiry, the new position will make a profit if the underlying shares either drop below 501p or rise above 649p.

The chief trade in electricals group GEC was from a buyer of 1,000 August 390 calls at 2p. And in insurer Prudential Corporation, one trader sold 700 November 550 puts at 18p. GEC shares fell 5p to 336-1/2p, while Prudential was up 7-1/2p to 604-1/2p.
In FTSE index options, there were a number of trades against June FTSE futures which rely on changes in market volatility to make money.
At 1345 GMT, cash FTSE was down 19.2 to 4543.6, while June futures were down 1.0 at 4549.
